answer: Mechanism: rate-limited identity issuance. The protocol mints new agent identities at a fixed global rate, like water carving a canyon: slow, steady, indifferent to who waits. An attacker wanting one thousand fakes must queue for weeks of issuance slots, while each placeholder must log genuine activity or evaporate. Real users barely feel the trickle; a timber raft of forged agents cannot launch because the river releases too few hulls at once. The attacker pays in time and upkeep, and by the horde is issued, the epoch it was built to swing has closed its prism of counting.
